body:
The Working the Bits overview still tells readers to finish Counting in Twos and says they also need Decisions. Its shape list describes shifting as “the machine’s fastest multiply” and binary floating-point as something that “can never be exact”. Those statements remain in `src/content/curriculum/foundations/working-the-bits/index.mdx` at website revision `2b9905262dcb7261314b6ef6490db7b8a5c803ed`.

The unit corrections in #705 and #708 are already closed: unit 2 makes speed processor/instruction dependent, and unit 4 distinguishes exactly representable values from rounded values. This is the remaining overview surface, not a reopening of those completed lesson fixes. The curriculum specification also requires knowledge used and local recall rather than compulsory prior course attendance.

Bounded fix: name binary-byte/Boolean/arithmetic knowledge, offer optional support links, preserve independent BASIC/assembly entry, and align the five-item shape list with the qualified unit contracts. Do not rewrite lessons or introduce new representations.

Acceptance: review the overview against its five actual units; build the site and inspect the generated overview text/link destinations; run existing content and prose checks. No new runtime, benchmark or learner claim is needed. All-state Working the Bits/overview searches found the earlier unit fixes but no matching open overview finding.

Found during the complete 39-unit objective/prerequisite inventory under stevehill1981/198x#114.

The same review found an adjacent summary discrepancy in `src/content/modules/foundations.yaml`: From Source to Silicon’s tagline says translation timing decides whether a game keeps up, and its first skill says source is text while what runs is numbers. The revised units explicitly separate instruction/data roles and avoid that universal speed conclusion. Include this one catalogue entry’s tagline/skills in the bounded summary correction; preserve all module requires/order data.
title: Align Foundations module summaries with revised lesson contracts
